title: Let generic code build a shipment without warnings

blocks.text: The warehouse service builds every shipment through `Shipment.of(...)`. The team turned on `-Xlint:unchecked -Werror`, and now the routing module, which ships one parcel of any type from a generic helper, no longer compiles: javac warns at its call to `Shipment.of`. A teammate's first fix also went wrong in production: the loading screen reuses one array for every truck, and shipments that had already left changed their parcels when the next truck was loaded.

items: `of(parcels)`: build the shipment from its parcels.

blocks.text: When you're done, generic code calls `of` without a warning, and a shipment's parcels stay what they were when `of` returned. About three lines in total, the method's declaration included.
The tests compile a generic caller with the JDK's compiler, against your class.

cases.says: a shipment holds its parcels in the order they were given
a generic helper gets back a shipment whose parcels read as the helper's type
a generic method that calls of compiles with -Xlint:unchecked and no unchecked warning
an array the caller passes and then reuses doesn't change the shipment built from it

origin.section: @SafeVarargs Removes the Warning at the Cause, and javac Doesn't Check the Promise

concepts: javac doesn't check the @SafeVarargs promise: a method that keeps or hands out its varargs array pollutes the heap, and the ClassCastException lands in code with no cast, away from the cause.
@SafeVarargs stops javac warning every caller about generic array creation, which @SuppressWarnings on the declaration doesn't do.
